worker-crash.method: Three actual subprocess os._exit deaths after committed native backend claim; default 30 second lease expires on real clock; frozen replacement EmbeddingWorker, exact precomputed Tencent native vectors; isolated synthetic clone. No SQL job status edits.

provider-faults.method: Actual loopback HTTP provider and frozen default worker timeout10s/lease30s. First request times out, returns429 Retry-After2, or503; actual persisted backoff then successful exact native precomputed vector. Three repeats each; no job state/clock edits.
provider-faults.limitation: Transient recovery only; HTTP exhaustion/dead-letter and search degradation require separate coverage.

provider-exhaustion.method: Actual loopback HTTP503 on every attempt, native max_attempts5 and real database backoff, three repetitions; no SQL job status/time edits.
provider-exhaustion.limitation: Search-degradation response semantics remain separate; dead-letter correctness does not prove all F3 requirements.

database-restart.limitation: Actual API writes during three Docker database restarts and acknowledged-row verification. Recovery is ten additional successful writes, not p95 returning to baseline; explicit retryable error semantics must be assessed from actual status counts. Performance acceptance not inferred.

log-leak-check.limitation: Only isolated successful search and validation rejection with console telemetry and dedicated proxy logs. Full pressure/fault collection and external collectors not yet covered. Intentional private LLM request/response archives excluded; these are required evidence, not operational logs.

database_restart_log_scan.coverage: three actual database restarts under acknowledged API writes; successful and failed requests; actual INFO logs, console traces and error stacks

tx2-results-audit.uncertainty_method: Exact27 resamples of3 independent API-process repeats with replacement; percentile95% interval. n=3 has low precision. Latency CI is the mean of per-repeat p95s, not a pooled per-request p95 CI.
interpretation: Use error count/request count, not the k6 Counter rate field, for error fractions.
All six load-host resource checks pass, but every run dropped arrivals; no sustainable1QPS capacity claim.
Slow lexical SQL and pool exhaustion are observed; this is not proof of a single root cause or an optimization result.
Server status and SQL logs include warmup and shutdown; client timeout and later server response counts cannot be directly equated.
Canceled query exceptions during cleanup can serialize SQL parameters containing full fictional queries. This fails the body-log requirement even though no real user conversation was used.
Both machines are in ap-shanghai. Independent-host public ingress was tested; cross-region path was not.
